methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Virginia’s technical workforce faces uncertainty as funding runs out for middle school program
signals.signal_reading: Loss of GO TEC funding in historically underserved Southside signals failure to build foundational technical literacy in regions already behind, deepening the preconditions for concentrated rather than distributed AI capability development.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free community AI workshops by a Norfolk native attempting to 'close the technology gap' represents grassroots peer-to-peer knowledge distribution outside traditional institutions, though sustainability and depth remain uncertain without institutional backing.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's formal partnership with AI Ready RVA concentrates institutional resources and expertise in Richmond metro, potentially deepening capability in the capital region while question of knowledge diffusion to surrounding areas remains unaddressed.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab launch creates institutional AI education capacity in a mid-tier region, but as a single-institution initiative signals concentrated rather than distributed capability building even within the Roanoke Valley.

signals.title: Va. job market faces AI challenge: high-achieving college grads 'having trouble getting jobs' - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: High-achieving college graduates struggling to find jobs as AI automates entry-level work suggests shallow platform-driven AI adoption by employers focused on displacement rather than workforce augmentation or deep capability building.
